subject: Dedicated capacity criteria & ops alignment — next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@glowai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity criteria & ops alignment — next steps

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned on the key operational and success criteria we heard from GlowAI: 

- Primary pain: unpredictable inference spend and latency variability during campaign peaks (marketing pushes and feature flags) leading to user-visible slowdowns.
- Current stack: GlowAI is running an in-house endpoint layer on AWS with mixed instance GPU autoscaling; model runtime today is a 13B decoder with average input ~320 tokens, 95th percentile sequence length ~700 tokens.
- Target SLA: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for median 512-token requests; sustained baseline of ~600 RPS with short peaks up to ~1,800 RPS (peaks typically 10–20 minute bursts).
- Isolation & compliance: must have logical isolation of customer workloads, separate networking for sensitive traffic, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.
- Autoscale/burst requirements: predictable reserved pool for baseline throughput + ability to burst up to 2.5x for short windows without throttling; predictable cold-start behavior for new model variants.
- Cost control levers: caching (prefix/KV), batching policies, and quantization profiles — GlowAI is open to quantization if quality stays within 3% of current BLEU-like evals.

Next steps we agreed: 
1) GlowAI to share a 72-hr trace + a sample payload schema and representative input batch (we requested anonymized / redacted inputs).
2) Redwood to run a quick sizing exercise and propose a reserved pool configuration + burst strategy.
3) Schedule a technical sizing workshop (SE-led) to validate memory/kv-cache needs and sequence-length distribution tradeoffs.
4) Share SOC2 snapshot and a draft MA proposal for procurement.

I've attached the capacity extract you mentioned (capacity-profile-extract.csv) and our SOC2 snapshot + a high-level MA draft for procurement review.

Proposed times for the sizing workshop: Tue Dec 2, 10–11 AM PT or Wed Dec 3, 2–3 PM PT. Marcus (cc'd) will lead the SE portion. Which works best for the GlowAI infra team?

Thanks — looking forward to the sizing workshop.

— Camila

Thanks Camila — this is a great summary. Confirming/clarifying a few points from the GlowAI side: 

- Numbers: baseline is ~600 RPS average (user-facing inference requests), but our campaign traffic historically has produced short bursts up to ~1,800 RPS for 10–25 minutes several times a week. We need to avoid queuing/503s during those windows.
- Latency SLO is p95 <= 200ms for requests with <=512 tokens; for longer fan-out tasks (internal batch jobs) we can accept higher latency.
- Isolation: procurement requires a logically dedicated pool (no cross-customer tenancy for our reserved capacity). We also need to know how we can prove isolation for audit.
- Autoscaling behavior: ideal is reserved baseline + defined burst pool with automatic fallback to lower-cost variants if the burst threshold persists >30 minutes.

I've attached the CSV with a 72-hr trace we pulled (capacity-profile-extract.csv) and a short infra diagram. Sanjeev will join the sizing call.

Wed Dec 3, 2–3 PM PT works best for us.

Olivia

Perfect — thanks for the trace, Olivia and Sanjeev. A few clarifying notes and items we'll bring to the Dec 3 workshop: 

- Marcus (SE) will run a short guided worksheet during the meeting to capture exact memory footprint, KV cache hit expectations, batching/latency tradeoffs, and useful quantization tolerances. We'll need a sample model artifact or a point-estimate of peak GPU memory usage if available.
- For isolation proofs: Redwood can provide architecture diagrams, tenancy configuration, and audit logs for dedicated pools; procurement typically accepts a SOC2 snapshot + a short isolation attestation we can prepare.
- For burst policy: we propose a baseline reserved pool sized to cover 70–80% of observed steady-state RPS and a burst-capacity policy that allows short automatic bursts to cover up to 2.5x peak for windows <30 minutes. For sustained excess we can configure an automatic fallback to a cheaper compatible model variant (e.g., 8-bit quantized) and an alerting workflow to notify GlowAI engineering and ops.

Pre-work (please send before Tue EOD PT if possible):
- 72-hr trace (received — thanks)
- Sample payload/avro/json schema (for batching simulation)
- Peak GPU memory estimate or model artifact pointer

I'll upload a short sizing worksheet link after this message; for now attaching the MA draft for procurement review. If procurement needs a specific format for an attestation, loop them in and we'll adapt.

See you Wed Dec 3, 2 PM PT. Marcus — can you prepare a quick checklist on inputs we need from the infra team?

Thanks,
Camila
